newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower on active selling.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower on active selling.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended lower on Monday, as the weaker Chicago corn market on Friday and the yen's stronger tone against the dollar discouraged local investors, traders said.
Prices were 60 to 220 yen lower. But the newly listed September contract closed at 15,170 yen per tonne, up by 170 yen from the opening. The estimated volume was 59,049 lots.
Local investors started selling actively from the opening session, traders said. The November 1997 and the July 1998 contract fell by their daily 400 yen limit in the early afternoon.
"But technical buying supported the market by the close," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system stood at $2.58-1/2 per bushel at 0850 GMT, against $2.60 from Friday's close.
Spot August CBOT soybean futures were at $7.88 per bushel at 0850 GMT, against $7.91-3/4 at Friday's close.
